parent.title: [Workstream] Continuous port pipeline
parent.body:
## User outcome

New and blocked ports move through research, catalog admission, automation, and hands-on qualification without expanding V1 by default.

## Current behavior and evidence

Re-read 2026-09-05 at main `d10c331d1d8a06b512f047f9ba5be721e1cfe4fa` and live Project/relationships for #267. Existing implementation and qualification evidence below is preserved; the automation-first scope is planned, not shipped. No new gameplay or physical observation was performed.

This is a shared workstream only. Every catalog entry and researched candidate is represented by exactly one independently movable durable repository issue; no mutable individual-port state lives here.

## Scope

Coordinate shared port-catalog engineering and dependency relationships. Individual issues own every port's upstream, identity, source, release, setup, persistence, stage, blockers, qualification, and completion evidence.

Integration completion is scoped to the promised supported operations and actual checks; optional gameplay research is separate unless a concrete regression makes it required. One durable issue per port is bookkeeping, not a per-release manual approval gate. #246 owns automatic admission/publication, #177 neutral observation and #254 assisted authoring. Existing Supported attestations remain true and unchanged.

## Non-goals

No frozen title list, catalog count target, fabricated checksums, source weakening, or global V1 blocker for every candidate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every independently catalogable or independently prioritizable port has exactly one durable GitHub issue and one Project entry classified as Port.
- [ ] Intake preserves existing parents, accepts unparented ports, and never depends on this workstream’s child capacity.
- [ ] Shared engineering and family issues coordinate ports but never replace individual issues.
- [ ] `roadmap doctor` reports no port-issue coverage drift.

## Required tests

Cataloged work uses the full catalog/source/lifecycle/qualification gates; research drafts require evidence review before promotion.

## Documentation impact

catalog.json remains actual support authority; dated source narratives remain archived.

## Dependencies and blockers

Each candidate records its own blocker and can proceed independently.

## Completion evidence

The continuous workstream remains open. On 2026-09-04, Pokémon Gold, Pokémon Silver, Pokémon Crystal, and Final Fantasy VII advanced from Manual qualification to Supported for Windows after the repository owner's hands-on attestation was recorded in https://github.com/boburning/portcove/pull/231. The PR merged as a366ea315b86cfe5a7a8f3cc867612b0ebed7732 and its post-merge main CI passed at https://github.com/boburning/portcove/actions/runs/33876486947.

<!-- portcove-origins: PCV-DEF-007 -->

<!-- portcove-reconciliation-2026-09-06 -->
## Port audit and discovery reconciliation — 2026-09-06

The September 5 inventory of 117 issues is historical. All 117 records are reconciled in the dated snapshot; 57 completed Windows Supported records retain their catalog-owned legacy intersection without redundant requalification. The approved follow-up uses [the Port Pipeline Project view](https://github.com/users/boburning/projects/1/views/4) as the complete inventory. Work type = Port and one canonical issue per independent port define coverage. Parent links are optional and preserved; this workstream's existing children are historical organization, not the full inventory. The 62 formerly missing parent links are no longer required. Use optional parents for bounded outcomes, not numbered overflow workstreams; genuine blockers remain explicit dependencies. Tooling and regression coverage are in PR #386.

First research order: REDRIVER2, SymphonyRecomp, Legacy of Darkness (only these three new discovery entries enter Next). CTR Native follows after its x86/raw-disc boundary is reviewed; Golden Balloon, Co-op DX, Sonic 3 A.I.R. and seven RetComM candidates remain a shortlist in Later, not fourteen implementation commitments. Prioritize reusable player outcomes/evidence/effort, not port count. The #15/#242 onboarding/storage sequence and Required #245/#246 Beta 1 proof remain protected. No catalog change or qualification is claimed.

This dated addition schedules future work; it supplies no new installation or gameplay evidence. Live placement remains in the Project. [Import evidence and source references](https://github.com/boburning/portcove/blob/feature/ports-roadmap-reconciliation-20260906/docs/archive/2026-09-06-ports-roadmap-reconciliation.md).
